transcript:
Header: 2026-03-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM), Lara Gomez (Meridian), Tom Reynolds (Meridian Eng Manager), Ibrahim Khan (Meridian Security), Nina Park (Meridian PM)

Summary: quick kickoff to align on onboarding, integration patterns, security checklist and pilot timeline.

00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, I'm Alex from Redwood, this is Samir our solutions engineer and Priya our CSM
00:08 Lara Gomez: hi thanks, excited to get started we had a couple of questions about where to host models and how data residency will work
00:15 Samir Patel: yeah great question, we'll walk through hosted vs dedicated vs private, and we can map that to your compliance needs
00:30 Tom Reynolds: for context, our stack is primarily AWS, k8s for services, we have a VPC and need to limit egress, also interested in latency numbers for chat workloads
00:42 Ibrahim Khan: security wise we need SOC2, audit logs, SSO with SAML, and keys in our KMS, we also have data retention policies so we need to confirm log retention and data deletion flows
00:56 Samir Patel: noted, Redwood support SSO SAML, RBAC and we integrate with customer KMS for private deployments, for hosted API we have encryption at rest but we can talk through dedicated where KMS integration is available
01:12 Alex Chen: and to set expectations we'll propose pilot: 2 weeks to validate quality and latency, then scale. Success metrics would be p95 latency under 250ms for inference, cost per 1k tokens under threshold, and no data leakage per security review
01:30 Lara Gomez: p95 250ms is ambitious—what's typical for hosted? also do you support quantized model variants for cost
01:40 Samir Patel: so typical p95 for small chat prompts on hosted is 120-300ms depending on load and model; dedicated lowers tail latency and gives predictable throughput; we also have quantization/compilation profiles to reduce cost, but we should run the benchmark on your dataset
02:05 Tom Reynolds: ok, how do we run that benchmark? we prefer not to share PHI in the test dataset, can we run with synthed data or pseudo-anonymized samples
02:17 Samir Patel: absolutely, synthed is fine. we'll give you a small harness, you'll run a pass and we collect token counts and latency metrics. If you want, we can run a parallel job on a dedicated pool if you sign a short reserved capacity trial
02:33 Ibrahim Khan: what's the contract surface for dedicated vs private, and do you have on-prem options? our compliance team might require air-gapped for certain workloads
02:45 Alex Chen: we have three modes: hosted API (fastest to start), dedicated (reserved GPU capacity with SLA), and private (VPC or on-prem for strict compliance). On-prem is possible but requires a license + deployment cadence, usually later in the journey
03:05 Nina Park: who's the single point of contact from Redwood for day-to-day onboarding
03:10 Priya Shah: that's me, Priya will run onboarding tasks, set up workspaces, and coordinate internal teams
03:18 Priya Shah: I'll share the onboarding checklist and calendar invites. also I'll set up a workspace in Redwood Console with your project
03:28 Tom Reynolds: good. what about logging and audit trails? our auditors need to see per-request logs and who accessed the model
03:36 Samir Patel: we emit request traces and token-level cost breakdowns in the console; for private deployments we can forward logs to your SIEM or to S3 in your account; we'll confirm retention windows and redaction options
03:50 Ibrahim Khan: and KMS, does Redwood support customer-managed keys in hosted mode? we prefer keys we control
03:56 Samir Patel: customer-managed KMS is available for private and dedicated, hosted can be discussed on a case-by-case basis but typically uses Redwood-managed keys; we can add exceptions in enterprise contracts
04:12 Lara Gomez: great, timeline—we'd like a pilot in two weeks, production in 8-10 weeks afterwards, is that feasible
04:20 Alex Chen: yes that's the typical cadence. We'll aim for pilot start 2026-03-22, and assuming success ramp to production in 8-10 weeks. we'll calendar out the milestones
04:35 Tom Reynolds: integration points: APIs, sdk, and do you have an operator for k8s or a helm chart if we go private
04:42 Samir Patel: for private we provide helm chart and operator and an infra repo example; for hosted it's REST + SDKs and we have an ingress pattern for VPC peering or private link
04:58 Nina Park: who signs off on success internally for us? it's me and Lara from product and data
05:05 Lara Gomez: yes, data and product will sign off, engineering will validate latency and infra
05:20 Alex Chen: ok next steps I'll send pricing and onboarding guide; Samir will set up technical deep dive and benchmark harness; Priya will invite you to the workspace
05:35 Ibrahim Khan: I'll send the security questionnaire and KMS requirements, expect that by 2026-03-15
05:48 Priya Shah: perfect, I'll follow up with an invite for next week for the technical deep dive, does Wednesday or Thursday work for you all
05:55 Tom Reynolds: Thursday works
06:00 Alex Chen: cool thanks everyone, we'll recap in an email with action items
06:05 [End of recording]
